summary: Date matcher misses legacy ISO-string eventDate setlists (= every current setlist).
repro: call list_musicians_on_date with any date that has a setlist on it (e.g. 2026-05-13 — the Shir Shabbat setlist Ikl0sS4XcZil0Z04viAu). also tried 2026-04-18, 2026-04-25, and full-ISO timestamp '2026-05-13T19:53:47.014Z'. all return matchedSetlists:[].
expected: the May 13 setlist (and any others on the day) should appear in matchedSetlists; assignments may legitimately be empty but the setlist match itself should fire.
root_cause_hint: git show origin/master:src/lib/mcp/tools/roster.ts:404-415 — the implementation queries Firestore via where('eventDate','>=',Timestamp.fromDate(...)). in-code comment acknowledges 'legacy rows may store the string ISO. ... can be matched via a follow-up grep if needed' — that follow-up was never implemented. all observed setlists in list_setlists return eventDate as ISO string in their payload, suggesting they're stored as strings.

summary: Same test-session cookie path hydrates useAuth().user for musician+band_leader test fixtures but NOT for the sound-engineer test fixture in the same probe run.
repro: mint test-session cookies for c9i4-musician, c9i4-band_leader, c9i4-soundengineer; navigate Playwright (separate browser contexts) to /monitor with each cookie; wait 6s.
observed: musician sees 'Monitor Access Denied' (the !hasAccess branch, after a non-null user). band_leader same. sound_engineer sees 'Sign in to access monitor controls' (the !user branch). Yet the SE's top nav DOES show the 'Monitor' link (meaning some server-side path KNOWS they're SE). Per META-003 the expected state is user=null for all 3 (no Web SDK signin) — so the surprise is that 2/3 hydrate.
expected: consistent behavior across roles given the same auth-bootstrap path.
caveat: single-shot sample per role; SE re-probe with extended wait was attempted but file-copy mojibake blocked the rerun. Could be timing/flake — flagging because the asymmetry is reproducible enough to merit a code look at the auth-context cookie-hydration branch.

summary: Concrete gap spec — what a band_leader CANNOT answer about tonight's roster via current MCP.
repro: compare PARENT §1's user stories ('Who's confirmed?', 'swap X for Y', 'notify the sub') against the 9 exported functions in roster.ts.
observed: gaps: (a) no notify_musician/nudge tool — pending invites can't be re-poked from MCP; (b) no atomic swap_musician — must do unassign+assign = 2 notification cascades; (c) listPendingAssignments lacks invitedAt/lastNotifiedAt so 'who's stale' is unanswerable; (d) no bulk_assign — 5-piece onboarding fires 5 separate cascades; (e) list_pending_assignments is admin/band_leader gated, so a musician using MCP cannot discover their OWN assignmentId — they must be GIVEN it; (f) no roster-history read ('what's the last 3 services Jake played'); (g) no broadcast_to_band tool; (h) terminal-status visibility is one-sided — declined/cancelled assignments don't surface in any list_* tool.
expected: these are net-new tools, not bugs. captured as a phase-spec.
